Scenario description (excerpt)
WestRock Company reports on its deferred tax assets and valuation allowances.  As of September 30, 2018 and September 30, 2017, gross net operating losses for foreign reporting purposes of approximately $698.4 million and $673.7 million, respectively, were available for carry-forward.  A majority of these loss carry-forwards generally expire between fiscal 2020 and 2038, while a portion have an indefinite carry-forward.  The tax-effected values of these net operating losses are $185.8 million and $182.6 million at September 30, 2018 and 2017, respectively, exclusive of valuation allowances of $161.5 million and $149.6 million at the same dates.  At September 30, 2018 and 2017, the company had state tax-credit carry-forwards of $64.8 million and $54.4 million, respectively.  These state tax-credit carry-forwards generally expire within five to ten years; however, certain state credits can be carried forward indefinitely.  Valuation allowances of $56.1 million and $47.3 million at September 30, 2018 and 2017, respectively, have been provided on these assets.  These valuation allowances have been recorded due to uncertainty regarding the company’s ability to generate sufficient taxable income in the appropriate taxing jurisdiction.  Consistent with prior years, management considers a portion of the earnings from certain foreign subsidiaries as subject to repatriation and provides for taxes accordingly.  However, all other unremitted earnings from foreign subsidiaries are considered indefinitely reinvested.  As of September 30, 2018, the estimated outside-basis difference in foreign subsidiaries considered indefinitely reinvested was approximately $1.5 billion.

  List acquisition transactions recorded in the database.
